about: Original lines the content engine draws on for posts that aren't built from live prices. All written in the house voice (golf-club banter, never mean, British). Add freely; the planner never reuses a set-up within 60 days. Myths must be true as written; nothing here invents a person's real story.

carousels.title: 5 things to check before you *buy a driver*
carousels.cover_sub: Save this for your next upgrade
slides: Get fitted first
Loft and shaft suit your swing more than the logo does. Many shops fit you free when you buy.
Last season's model
New drivers launch early in the year, and last season's tend to get cheaper once they do.
Check the price history
A sale price only means something if you know what it usually costs.
Compare more than one shop
The same driver can cost very different amounts at different UK retailers.
close: Follow for golf banter, real deals and the odd useful tip.

carousels.title: How to *stop losing* so many balls
slides: Watch it all the way down
Pick a landmark where it lands before you look away.
Club down near trouble
Less club off the tee often means more balls in your bag at the end.
Play the right ball
A durable, softer two-piece ball suits most club golfers and costs less to lose.
Buy in bulk at the right time
Balls are cheaper by the dozen and often cheapest in winter sales.
close: Tag the mate who needs it most.

carousels.title: Winter golf: *what you actually need*
slides: Waterproofs first
A proper waterproof jacket and trousers beat any number of jumpers.
Layers, not bulk
A thin base layer and a midlayer let you swing freely and stay warm.
Winter gloves
Rain gloves get grippier when wet. Keep a dry pair in the bag.
Mittens between shots
Warm hands make a real difference to feel on the greens.
close: Save this for the *next cold snap*
Follow for more ways to play more and pay less.

myths.title: Myth: a new driver will *fix your slice*
slides: MYTH
A new driver fixes a slice
The swing path causes a slice. A driver set up with more draw bias or loft can reduce it a bit, but it won't cure it.
TRUTH
Fitting helps more than a new head
A fitting matches loft, lie and shaft to your swing. A lesson or two helps most of all.
TIP
Last season's model is often enough
If you are buying, last season's version usually performs very close to the new one for less.
close: Got a golf myth you want busted? Drop it in the comments.

myths.title: Myth: Black Friday is *always* cheapest
slides: MYTH
Black Friday prices are always the lowest
Some are genuine lows. Some are the usual price with a new label.
TRUTH
Check the history
We check every price against what it cost in October, so the real deals stand out.
TIP
Set a price alert
If it isn't low enough yet, an alert tells you when it drops, whatever the date.

myths.title: Myth: expensive balls are *wasted* on you
slides: MYTH
Premium balls are only for good players
Premium balls do give more spin around the greens for everyone.
TRUTH
It depends how many you lose
If you lose a few a round, a cheaper ball you can afford to lose may suit you better.
TIP
Find your middle ground
Mid-priced urethane balls are a good balance, and dozens are cheapest bought in bulk.

characters.name: Big Dave
characters.look: Broad, cheerful fifty-something, ruddy cheeks, short greying hair, neat grey beard, navy quarter-zip, beige trousers, white cap, white golf shoes.
characters.personality: Society captain. Loud, optimistic, totally oblivious. Owns every gadget, has never once hit a fairway.
quirks: generous with his own scorecard (six is a par if you squint)
blames the course, the wind, the ball, the greenkeeper
announces every drive as 'the one'
first to the bar, last to the tee

characters.name: Phil
characters.look: Lean fifty-something, clean-shaven, tweed flat cap, olive quilted gilet over a white polo, wristwatch.
characters.personality: Dave's long-suffering mate. Deadpan, says almost nothing; his eyebrows do the talking.
quirks: keeps the real score
arrives with the perfect prop (abacus, calculator, rule book, rake)
arms folded = verdict delivered
the only one who reads the local rules

characters.name: Steady Steve
characters.look: Tall, thin, sixty-something, short white hair, beige windproof jacket, faded bucket hat, old leather carry bag.
characters.personality: Plays the same 20-year-old irons, never loses a ball, never buys anything. 180 yards, dead straight, every single time.
quirks: tea from a thermos on the 10th
still uses a pencil from 2004
wins the society cup without anyone noticing
the receipts guy: knows what everything should cost

characters.name: Gaz
characters.look: Thirty-something, fresh haircut, bright plain teal top, black cap with sunglasses perched on it, brand-new everything (no logos).
characters.personality: Buys a new driver every spring, blames the old one. Knows every launch date and none of his yardages.
quirks: 'it's the shaft, mate'
unboxes kit in the car park
has three rangefinders and still asks Phil
always 'just looking' at the pro shop

characters.name: Kev
characters.look: Stocky forty-something, ginger stubble, cheeky grin, plain burgundy jumper, grey trousers, black bobble hat in winter (plain grey cap in summer).
characters.personality: Can't help himself. Cracks a one-liner after every bad shot, pulls faces, and is always in the background trying (and failing) not to laugh when someone duffs, thins or shanks one.
quirks: shoulders shaking, hand over mouth, in the back of the shot
commentary voice: 'and it's... gone'
slow clap for a ball that finally gets airborne
his own shots are no better, and everyone remembers
characters.use: Reaction shots of Kev (stifled laugh, hand over mouth, slow clap, wince, fake commentary mic) are reusable: cut one in after any duff, thin or misplaced shot in a sketch. Keep them in the library tagged kev plus the reaction.

charactersAbout: Recurring, obviously fictional characters (AI-generated photos, never based on real people). Keep looks identical in every photo; build running gags across episodes; never mean-spirited: everyone gets a win sometimes. Kev's ribbing is always friendly, and he gets his comeuppance too.

runningGags.about: Kev knows Gaz is a kit addict. Friendly banter only, never bullying: Gaz gives as good as he gets, and sometimes the new kit actually works.
kev: Must need a new driver, Gaz.
Did it come with a lesson?
Bet it goes further in the box.
gaz: Says the man with a 2009 rangefinder.
Laugh all you like, it's last season's, I paid less.
At least mine went in the air, Kev.
